phase_name: Authority Evaluation Model Implementation Contract Freeze
summary: Phase 147E converts Phase 147D's implementation architecture into AEMIC-001 v1.0 (docs/contracts/AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT.md), a binding, falsifiable implementation contract for the standalone pcae.authority_evaluation package, independently re-derived from AEM-001, Phase 147C, Phase 147D, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, CHGR-001, TAMC-001/TAMPC-001, GAC-001, the Decision Template and Human Governance Record schemas, and direct re-inspection of src/pcae/interactive_workflow/persistence/{repository.py,filesystem_repository.py}, src/pcae/governance/publication/coordinator.py, and tests/test_phase_144c_publication_coordinator.py's AST-enforced forbidden-import boundary -- treating Phase 147D's own prose as design-intent evidence, never as contractual authority in its own right, classifying every 147D design choice explicitly as Required, Permitted-and-elected, Recommended-and-adopted, or Deferred-not-bound (Contract Sec.1.1). Freezes the package boundary (src/pcae/authority_evaluation/, six required modules -- models, evaluation, registry, errors, serialization, plus a re-export-only __init__ -- and a forbidden-import list wider than Phase 147D named, additionally covering pcae.commands/pcae.cli/pcae.core/pcae.lifecycle/pcae.repository_intelligence alongside interactive_workflow/governance/cltr, confirmed against the actual current src/pcae/ directory listing). Freezes the public domain model -- EligibleAuthorityDeclaration (six fields, closed shape), AuthorityEvaluationOutcome (eight fields), EvaluationResult (closed three-member enum) -- adding a construction-time invariant this phase itself introduces: citation_text is non-None exactly when evaluation_result equals eligible, converting AEM-REQ-018's own field description into a mechanically enforced, falsifiable rule. Translates AEM-001's disclosure-only principle into a binding naming/documentation requirement (authorize/grant/permit/allow/deny-named functions or types are prohibited anywhere in the package's public API). Reconciles F-147C-1 at the implementation level (the existing decision_template.schema.json eligible_authority field remains the sole citation-text source, copied verbatim at evaluation time rather than referenced, since a reference would violate the outcome's own immutability and reconstructibility guarantees) while explicitly naming two limitations rather than silently resolving them: how a future caller obtains citation text absent any DecisionTemplate Python artifact, and that this package performs zero consistency validation between a Declaration's eligible_identities set and its sibling template's free-text field (restating FA-147D-3's own non-policy-language judgment call). Freezes identity as the (template_ref, template_version) tuple, never Session.template_ref alone. Closes Finding FA-147D-2 architecturally with a typed, three-way, mutually exclusive Registry-availability contract: None for absent Declaration, AuthorityRegistryUnavailableError for an unreachable store, AuthorityRegistryCorruptError for a reachable-but-malformed or duplicate record -- prohibiting first-match selection among duplicate candidates outright. Resolves, as this phase's own genuinely open design question (Phase 147D itself titled its own Sec.6.4 'architected, not built' without deciding the scope question), that a concrete filesystem Registry implementation is deferred past this contract's first-implementation scope, by direct analogy to the SessionRepository (Phase 143K, ABC only) / FilesystemSessionRepository (Phase 145D, later, separately-governed concrete implementation) precedent -- while pre-freezing that future concrete implementation's own persistence contract (storage root .pcae/authority-declarations/, atomic-write via tempfile.mkstemp plus os.fsync plus os.replace, path-safety and symlink rejection reusing the pattern without a cross-package import) for whichever future phase builds it. Freezes a six-exception failure taxonomy (four domain/structural, two Registry-infrastructure), a security contract restating every AEM-001 property preserved, an auditability contract distinguishing stable from observational outcome fields, a serialization contract with a reasoned digest-not-required decision for v1.0, and a deferred-integration boundary carrying Finding FA-147D-1 forward as an explicit, binding, unresolved precondition (an eight-step future sequence named purely as planning context, never authorized here). Produces a 14-row Requirement/Test Matrix (AEMIC-001 Sec.22) mapping every AEMIC-REQ identifier to a positive and, where applicable, negative/adversarial test, covering all sixteen required future test classes. Zero Blocking findings; zero unresolved implementation-critical decisions (AEMIC-001 Sec.20). Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT FROZEN WITH OBSERVATIONS. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147E_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_FREEZE.md.
